en: Puggalapaññatti Mātikā 5.
Pañcakauddesa (The Enumeration of Fives)
There are five types of persons:

There is a certain person who undertakes [an action] and feels remorse, yet does not understand, as it really is, that liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom wherein those arisen evil unwholesome states cease without remainder.

There is a certain person who undertakes [an action] but does not feel remorse, yet does not understand, as it really is, that liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom wherein those arisen evil unwholesome states cease without remainder.

There is a certain person who does not undertake [the practice] and feels remorse, yet he does not understand, as it really is, that liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom wherein those arisen evil unwholesome states cease without remainder.

There is a certain person who neither undertakes [the practice] nor feels remorse, yet he does not understand, as it really is, that liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom wherein those arisen evil unwholesome states cease without remainder.

There is a certain person who neither initiates [unwholesome actions] nor feels remorse, and he understands, as it truly is, that liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom wherein those arisen evil unwholesome states cease without remainder.

There are five types of persons comparable to warriors: one who gives and then despises; one who despises through living together; one who is a ready vessel for instruction; one who is fickle; and one who is dull and utterly deluded.
Five were alms-food eaters;
five were those who do not accept food after the meal has been prepared;
five were those who eat at a single sitting.
Five who wear robes made of rags from refuse heaps;
five who possess only three robes;
five who dwell in the forest.
Five who dwell at the foot of trees;
five who dwell in the open air;
five who remain in the sitting posture.
Five are those who accept whatever seat is offered.
Five are those who dwell in cemeteries.
This is the group of five.
